questions.q: The electrophile that attacks the phenoxide ion in the Reimer–Tiemann reaction is:
questions.explain: OH⁻ removes the proton of CHCl₃ and CCl₃⁻ loses Cl⁻ (α-elimination) to give neutral but electron-deficient dichlorocarbene.

questions.q: Phenol is heated with CCl₄ and aqueous NaOH, then acidified. The main product is:
questions.explain: Using CCl₄ instead of CHCl₃ introduces –COOH rather than –CHO, so phenol gives 2-hydroxybenzoic acid.

questions.q: Pyrrole is treated with chloroform and KOH. The product is:
questions.explain: In the abnormal Reimer–Tiemann reaction, :CCl₂ adds across a C=C and the ring expands by one carbon, keeping a chlorine (Ciamician–Dennstedt rearrangement).

questions.q: Which substrate is LEAST suitable for Reimer–Tiemann formylation?
questions.explain: Dichlorocarbene needs a very electron-rich ring such as a phenoxide ion; benzene itself is not attacked.
